recentItems.description:

Drive
By Katie O'Hara LaBrie
00-52125
MMSO Symphony Orchestra
Grade: 4
Take your ensemble on a musical road trip with Drive, an energetic overture that captures the spirit of innovation, adventure, and connection. With its infectious rhythms, nods to Gershwin, and soaring Americana-inspired themes, the piece celebrates the joy of the journey as much as the destination. An exhilarating work for full orchestra by Katie O'Hara LaBrie!

Danza Fuoco
By Kirt Mosier
00-50380
Highland String Orchestra
Grade: 4
Danza Fuoco is an exciting "fiery" dance that was inspired by the use of 7/8 rhythms and multi-meters. This piece was commissioned by Peter Lipari to commemorate Joliet Township's celebration of 120 years of orchestra. Every instrument is active throughout this work and takes the listener on an exciting journey through multi-meter South American dances to thought-provoking melodic beauty.

recentItems.description:
For more information, or to purchase, go to https://bit.ly/423wS09.

Furioso
By Todd Stalter (ASCAP)
00-50345
Belwin Intermediate String Orchestra
Grade: 2
Furioso, by Todd Stalter, is music that contains so much energy, it has to be released... but not all at once. After the opening statement, the music suddenly pulls back and begins a series of character shifts, each one building to another release of energy along the way. Changes in mood, texture, and musical dialogues between different parts of the string orchestra abound, adding variety, along with a sense that we are always heading towards a return of that explosive theme.

Students will use C naturals, slurs, double stops, G and C string notes, and first violins will use their E string. A perfect and mature-sounding piece that is accessible to younger players and will surely show off your beginning orchestra's abilities.

recentItems.description:
For more information, or to purchase, go to https://bit.ly/4sA1j98.

Mount Everest
By Rossano Galante
00-50333
Belwin Symphonic Full Orchestra
Grade: 4
This programmatic work embarks on a musical journey to the summit of the world's highest peak, Mt. Everest. The piece opens with a bold trumpet statement, supported by rhythmic ostinati in the winds, setting the stage for an ascent both daring and triumphant. The main theme, first introduced in the horns, is later taken up by the trumpets with a soaring horn obligato. A reflective, lyrical passage offers a moment of serenity before the music builds toward a powerful recapitulation. The piece culminates in a grand, majestic fanfare, evoking the awe-inspiring grandeur of Everest. This orchestral arrangement was inspired by composer Chris Bernotas.

Celestial Collisions
By Dión Morales
00-50339
Belwin Concert String Orchestra
Grade: 3
Celestial Collisions, by Dión Morales, is the overture to an epic space opera! The piece begins with a powerful rhythmic motif that pulls you into a story where danger lurks at every moment as sinister factions across the stars collide in the hopes of rising to power, gaining control, and bending the galaxy to their will. Our brave heroes fight for loved ones past and present in a struggle to bring peace to their worlds. Can our heroes survive? Will they find allies to join the fight? And will the universe finally find peace after these Celestial Collisions...

recentItems.title: God Rest Ye Merry, Gentlemen, arr. Alan A. Craig – Score & Sound
recentItems.description:
For more information, or to purchase, go to https://bit.ly/4cC8Bo5.

God Rest Ye Merry, Gentlemen
Traditional, arr. by Alan A. Craig
00-50381
Highland Full Orchestra
Grade: 4
The accent is placed on merry in Alan A Craig's joyful new orchestral arrangement of the much-loved Christmas carol God Rest Ye Merry, Gentlemen. Directors and players alike may find it impossible to resist the celebratory spirit of the rollicking rhythms and modal harmonies built into this vivid technicolor reboot of a centuries-old English festive folk song. The carol's popularity through the ages is reflected in fleeting musical echoes of urban Salvation Army bands, the fast-moving digital age, and, of course, the ancient Middle Eastern origins of its narrative. The arrangement also includes a part for optional unison voices, giving the opportunity for choirs or even audiences to loudly join in as the occasion dictates!
